title: Final week of early voting begins as record-breaking numbers highlight week one

 Final week of early voting begins as record-breaking numbers highlight week one 
 After days of record-breaking numbers, voters have one more week to cast their ballots early in the midterm election. By Nick Natario Monday, October 26, 2026 12:33PM Share HOUSTON, Texas (KTRK) -- After days of record-breaking numbers, voters have one more week to cast their ballots early in the midterm election.
 Harris County has broken early voting records, with more than 624,000 people casting ballots either in person or by mail during the first week of early voting, according to the elections office.
 Nearly 41,000 people voted in person on Sunday, the most for a seventh day of early voting in a midterm election.
 Democratic candidates have pointed to the numbers with optimism, while Republican candidates say a shift is coming in the second week.
 "I think people are already excited about the election. Lots of people are voting early, and I just can't wait until November 3rd," said Vicki Goodwin, a Democratic candidate for lieutenant governor.
 Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick, the Republican candidate for lieutenant governor, said his side still has ground to make up.

 "The Democrats are going to start running out of voters mid-week next week in terms of likely voters. We still have 600,000 high propensity voters that have not voted yet," Patrick said.
 The high turnout is not limited to Harris County. Secretary of State data show Fort Bend County leading the area, with 27% of registered voters already casting a ballot. Brazoria County, Austin County, and Galveston County are not far behind.
 There will be no voting this weekend. Early voting continues through Friday, and Election Day is Tuesday, Nov. 3.
 Voting sites are open from 7 a.m. until 7 p.m.
